question.text: Angel Funds (a sub-category of Cat I Venture Capital Funds) enjoy a distinct investor regime. What is the CORRECT position regarding investor requirements in Angel Funds?

answer.text: Angel Funds are subject to the same 1,000 investor cap as other AIFs
Angel Funds are capped at 200 investors under the Companies Act
Angel Funds shall not launch schemes, must onboard at least 5 accredited investors before first close, and each investment must have contribution from at least 2 accredited investors
Angel Funds have no minimum investor count

explanation.text: The Logic: Angel Funds operate under a distinct regime within Category I AIFs. The workbook states that Angel Funds raise money from accredited investors, shall not launch schemes, must onboard at least 5 accredited investors before first close, and that each investment requires contribution from at least 2 accredited investors. These limits replace the 1,000-investor per-scheme cap that applies to regular AIF schemes on page 504. The Trap: Option A applies the general AIF scheme cap incorrectly to Angel Funds. Option B conflates the Companies Act private placement cap. Option D is incorrect because the source sets specific accredited-investor minimums for Angel Funds. Note: Source pages 504 and 514-516 give the regular AIF scheme cap and the distinct Angel Fund regime including the no-schemes rule, the five-accredited-investor first-close requirement and the two-accredited-investor per-investment requirement.
